v1.feedback: Strong concept marriage — thin-film shimmer settling into the dark grooves of a Riley wave pattern is a genuinely poetic reading of 'iridescence.' The 30% saturation mix keeps the nacre restrained, and the 14s bloom cycle is unhurried. To refine: the diagonal sweep could be slower (uTime * 0.3 feels slightly rushed against the calm wave); consider letting the iridescence linger 1-2s longer in the envelope (widen the smoothstep window to 0.45–0.85) so viewers register the color before it fades. The twist parameter occasionally collapses the grid into near-uniform density — clamp uTwist to ±2.5 to preserve readable wave bands.

v2.feedback: The Riley-to-iridescence concept lands well — thin-film nacre bleeding into the dark interference bands is a genuine surprise moment tied to the parent's DNA. Two refinements: the iridescence bloom at 30% saturation mix is so subtle it risks being invisible on many monitors; consider raising to 0.40–0.45 and narrowing the diagonal sweep band so the color reads as a traveling ribbon rather than a global tint. Second, the white-on-white op-art flatness, while faithful to Riley, misses the gallery's contemplative register — an ivory or warm-bone background (0xf5f0e8) and charcoal bands instead of pure black would give it the aged-paper warmth the collection favors without betraying the source.
